**New evidence gathered this session:**
1. **Wrong-location root cause confirmed from v94 logs** (`/Users/zzl/PycharmProjects/vad/video_anomaly_detection/iteration_logs/results/v94_full_run.log`): fallback path scans only 6/43, 6/32, 6/33 segments with provably-noise prescreen scores (std=0.001-0.005); directed path scans 10/50 on Shoplifting004 with all candidates landing in the first 74s of a 222s video. My per-video IoU analysis of `/Users/zzl/PycharmProjects/vad/results/batch_eval_v94/`: 15/52 abnormal videos at IoU<0.05, and 10 of 15 are in the DIRECTED path — so any fix gated to the flat-CLIP fallback would miss two-thirds of the problem.
2. **MIL v6 localization killed with data**: offline eval on 140 abnormal test videos using precomputed features (`/Users/zzl/PycharmProjects/vad/features/test/`) — MIL v6 frame-level AUC 0.533-0.548, WORSE than MIL v1 (0.606-0.665), peak-in-GT only 26-27%. Anti-collapse training created variance uncorrelated with GT, definitively explaining the V80-V85b failure chain and eliminating MIL-guided candidates/fusion and snippet-resolution ideas.
3. **Comparative scan history**: v56's mechanism was mAP-positive (+0.006) but was buried by v58's threshold change and v61's bundled revert; the v57 non-exclusive schema at 0.3 threshold remains in the code, never tested at full coverage.
4. **Latency math**: mean 26.4 segments/video → ~3.7 comparative calls vs current 10-18 independent calls — fewer calls, full coverage, latency-neutral-to-positive.

Expected gain +0.03-0.06 mAP (0.18-0.21), attacking the largest validated bottleneck (28.8% wrong-location candidates) while leaving the v51 half-max curve, detection-count mechanics, and all downstream stages byte-identical.

A returned no proposal, so there is nothing to critique or merge. Decision: proceed with B's proposal (FCCS) unchanged. For the record, my self-audit against the four criteria:

(a) Failure modes: FCCS does not touch FM1 (relative_scores, 0.75/0.25 MIL fusion, v51 half-max crossing, v95/v96 modulators are byte-identical — verified the boundary path consumes frame_scorer.get_category_scores, computed independently of Stage 4 scan routing). FM2: detection-count machinery (top_k=3, _merge_adjacent, NMS 0.3, conf gates) unchanged; calibration should shrink, not grow, junk candidates. FM3: single deterministic call per batch, no temperature diversity. FM4: no revote on fixed decisions — this is upstream candidate generation, the same stage the v56 comparative scan (measured +0.006) operated at. Not a repeat of v78/v81/v92: those injected new signals or flipped inclusion decisions post-hoc; FCCS reuses the same VLM on the same segments, changing only coverage and judgment mode. Code anchors verified in repo: scan_segments_comparative (anomaly_discovery.py:50), _parse_comparative_response (:114), _merge_adjacent (:288), Stage 4 branch (pipeline.py:827-831), _directed_llm_scan (:1231).

(b) Architecture-level: yes — it replaces the candidate-generation scan architecture (directed partial-coverage independent judging → full-coverage comparative judging), not a threshold/weight. Switch-gated via config.py with prior behavior restored at False.

(c) Gain plausibility: expected 0.18-0.21 vs 0.1494 baseline; the keep-threshold >=0.17 sits above the ±0.03 noise band, and the smoke-gate (candidate-overlap recovery on Stealing036/Robbery050/Vandalism015) gives a cheap directional signal before spending a full eval. Floor case 0.16-0.17 is honestly ambiguous vs noise — the revert rule (<0.135 revert, 0.135-0.17 revert unless smoke showed clear recovery) handles it.

(d) Latency: call count drops 3-4x (mean ~3.7 calls/video vs 10-18); image tokens rise on mid videos but per-request overhead dominates; >60-segment videos capped at batch=16×1 keyframe. Net expected -5 to +10 s vs the 128s budget.

One refinement I'd adopt unilaterally: run the smoke gate with the switch on AND off in the same session to control for VLM drift before the full eval.

structured.risks: (1) Candidate-pool modification is historically the riskiest category (v78 confusion-negatives -0.04, v81 MIL-TAG bundled failure, v92 revoting -0.03). FM1 curve-shape: untouched — relative_scores, MIL fusion, half-max crossing byte-identical. FM2 detection-count: top_k/merge/NMS/gates unchanged bound the downside; calibration should REDUCE junk candidates; residual risk is fewer candidates on videos where junk-flagging accidentally included the true segment — covered by the smoke recall guard. structured.literature: (1) TimeChat (CVPR 2024), VTimeLLM (CVPR 2024), Momentor — video-LLM temporal grounding improves when the model reasons over broader temporal context rather than classifying isolated clips (the basis of the v56 comparative scan, validated positive internally: +0.006 mAP, confirmed in pipeline.py docstring). (5) LLM-as-a-judge comparative calibration (Zheng et al. 2023, MT-Bench lineage) — relative/paired judgments calibrate better than absolute per-item scores. (6) Learning Event Completeness (ICML 2025, arXiv 2506.13095 — verified via live search) — trained boundary modeling reaches only ~13.6% avg mAP@0.1-0.5 on UCF-Crime with CLIP features, confirming our 14.9% at harder thresholds is near the trained frontier and that boundary-side work has little headroom vs candidate-location work. structured.risks: (1) Main regression vector: on currently-TP videos where the VLM extent is WIDER than GT (VLM flags build-up/aftermath), a vlm_fit-driven wider proposal could drop IoU from e.g. 0.6 to 0.45 — gaining nothing at 0.3 but losing the 0.5/0.7 match. Mitigations: the multiplicative contrast term keeps core-anchored proposals competitive whenever the CLIP curve is sharply peaked (vlm_fit dominates only when the curve is flat/broad — exactly the cases where half-max is least reliable); the 10% hysteresis requires a clear joint-criterion win; duration_fit penalizes extents violating the category prior (verified on RoadAccidents125: 46.5s VLM extent gets dur_fit 0.43 vs max_dur 20, J ties the half-max proposal, hysteresis keeps half-max). Smoke gate explicitly checks no regression on currently-correct videos. (2) Why this avoids the v59/v65 boundary-replacement regressions: those had systematic one-directional narrowing bias applied unconditionally; CABS is symmetric (IoU-based vlm_fit and duration_fit push wider OR narrower by evidence), keeps half-max in the evaluated set, and is margin-gated. (3) Why it avoids FM1: no change to the fused curve, fusion weights, or half-max computation — only selection among proposals, with v54's kept duration-aware selection as precedent (CABS activates its dead 'combined' field and adds the completeness term). (4) VLM comparative scores are batch-calibrated (relative within contiguous batches); binarizing at the existing 0.3 candidacy threshold keeps semantics consistent with candidate generation — no new magic number. (5) 6s/4.5s-stride extent quantization is too coarse to help short events (GT 3-8s) but duration_fit + hysteresis neutralize it there; the mechanism targets long events where quantization is fine. (6) FCCS-off configs get vlm_fit=1.0 (neutral) — no cross-switch corruption.
structured.latency_impact: Strictly neutral: zero extra VLM calls, zero extra CLIP encodings. The completeness signal (per-segment comparative scores) is already produced by v97's FCCS and currently discarded — stashing it is O(n) memory only. Dense proposal evaluation is cumsum-vectorized: worst case ~4k pairs x 3 scales x 3 candidates of O(1) work, <10ms/video. This matters because v97 already exceeded the latency budget (141.5s vs ~128s); CABS adds nothing, keeping the door open to pair it with a future latency recovery loop.
structured.literature: (1) BMN — Boundary-Matching Network (Lin et al., ICCV 2019, arXiv 1907.09702): dense evaluation of ALL (start,end) proposal pairs via a boundary-matching confidence map whose value predicts completeness (IoU/IoF with the true event extent); final score = completeness x start/end boundary probabilities. Borrowed: dense (s,e) evaluation + the product form completeness x boundary-quality; our vlm_fit is the training-free completeness reference replacing the trained BM map. (2) BSN (Lin et al., ECCV 2018): boundary-sensitive proposal features (start/center/end zones) and pairing of start/end peaks around the actionness peak. Borrowed: peak-anchored proposal grid (lo <= peak <= hi). (3) Learning Event Completeness for Weakly Supervised VAD (ICML 2025, arXiv 2506.13095 — verified live): names partial-event detection (sub-windows) as THE WSVAD bottleneck and models completeness via anomaly-aware Gaussian mixtures; its ~13.6% avg mAP@0.1-0.5 trained on UCF-Crime confirms both the mechanism direction and that our 16.2% at harder thresholds is near the trained frontier — boundary-side completeness is the remaining headroom. (4) AutoLoc (Shou et al., ECCV 2018): Outer-Inner-Contrast — already our contrast term; CABS embeds it unchanged as one factor. (5) Holmes-VAU (CVPR 2025 Highlight, arXiv 2412.06171 — verified): segment-level MLLM anomaly scores as the localization signal for long videos; supports using the VLM per-segment curve as the coarse extent reference. (6) FreeZAD / Training-Free Zero-Shot TAD (arXiv 2501.13795, 2025 — fetched): threshold-merge + LogOIC + FFT calibration, 10-14 mAP THUMOS — confirms curve-only training-free scoring plateaus, motivating a SECOND (VLM) signal for completeness rather than more curve-only scoring; its LogOIC component was already tried here (v65/v66). (7) Internal, re-verified: v97 FCCS (kept, +0.0123; produces the per-segment score curve this idea consumes), v54 (duration-aware selection documented but contrast-only in code — CABS completes it), v96 (BSN-style directional boundary quality validated as a real signal, kept as confidence modulator), v59/v65 (one-directional boundary replacements regressed — CABS is symmetric and hysteresis-gated by contrast).

rawResult.content:
Proposal submitted via StructuredOutput. Summary of the work:

**Key code-verified discovery (root cause of the v97 lesson):** In the v97 FCCS comparative scan, `_comparative_call` (`/Users/zzl/PycharmProjects/vad/video_anomaly_detection/anomaly_discovery.py:110-113`) gets all ~12 frames of each 6s segment back from `SemanticFrameSampler` (since `compute_target_frames(6s)=18 >= 12`, no sampling occurs), then slices `keyframes[:2]` — so every 6s segment is shown to the VLM as only its first 0.5s (frames at t=0.0s and t=0.5s; a single t=0.0s frame for long videos). I verified this numerically. This explains exactly why v97's full coverage failed to recover the ~15 zero-IoU wrong-location videos: the true events are literally not in the images the VLM judges from.

**Proposed idea (v98): Dynamics-Guided Evidence Allocation (DGEA)** — replace the [:k] head-frame slice with dynamics-guided, segment-spanning keyframe selection under a fixed per-call image budget:
- Per-frame dynamics d(t) = 0.5·minmax(tsm_novelty) + 0.5·minmax(motion_energy), both already computed in `video_data` (zero new model/VLM calls)
- Per-video image budget kept exactly at v97 level (latency-neutral by construction), reallocated across segments proportional to dynamics (min 1, cap 4)
- Within each segment, pick top-k frames at dynamics peaks instead of the head slice
- Single config switch (`discovery.dynamics_guided_keyframes`, default off = byte-identical v97); touches only `config.py`, `anomaly_discovery.py`, `pipeline.py` (constructor + docstring), `batch_evaluate.py`

This is the training-free analog of Holmes-VAU's Anomaly-focused Temporal Sampler (CVPR 2025) and ReVisionLLM's coarse-to-fine focusing (CVPR 2025), avoids all 4 failure modes by construction, and is the first change targeting the evidence itself rather than a decision rule. Expected +0.015-0.04 mAP (target 0.175-0.20), latency-neutral.

Also flagged for the orchestrator: the archived v97 run logs in `iteration_logs/results/` show directed-scan lines and zero FCCS lines (likely mislabeled log copies — the +13.9s latency delta and eval JSON confirm FCCS ran); worth a quick verification before the next loop.

structured.title: Dynamics-Guided Evidence Allocation (DGEA): budget-fixed, stratified dynamics-guided keyframe selection for the FCCS comparative scan (joint consensus: B's proposal adopted with 2 robustness refinements; A's CABS explicitly sequenced as the next loop)
structured.mechanism:
CODE-RE-VERIFIED ROOT CAUSE (re-checked this session): in v97's FCCS scan, `_comparative_call` (anomaly_discovery.py:110-113) calls `_sample_keyframes`, which for a 6s segment returns ALL ~12 extracted frames (extraction fps=2 per config.py:134; compute_target_frames(6s)=18 >= 12 with fps_sample=3.0 per batch_evaluate.py:178, so no pre-sampling occurs; `_semantic_deduplicate` preserves temporal order via `selected_indices.sort()` at token_compressor.py:171), then slices `keyframes[:2]` (or [:1] for >60-segment videos). Net effect: every 6s segment is shown to the VLM as only its first ~0.5s. Events not overlapping a segment's head are invisible to the scan regardless of coverage or judgment mode — the concrete mechanism behind v97's failed wrong-location recovery ("cannot discriminate the true segment from temporal neighbors at batch granularity").

THE CHANGE (one config switch, `discovery.dynamics_guided_keyframes`, default False = byte-identical v97): replace the [:k] head-slice with dynamics-guided, segment-spanning keyframe selection under a FIXED per-video image budget. (1) Per-frame dynamics curve d(t) = 0.5*minmax(tsm_novelty) + 0.5*minmax(motion_energy), both already in video_data (pipeline.py:787, :793) before Stage 4 — zero new model/VLM calls, read-only. (2) Budget reallocation: per-video image budget kept EXACTLY at v97 level (N_segments x comparative_keyframes, or N x 1 under the >60-segment rule, so per-call image totals of 16 and call counts are unchanged by construction); every segment gets 1 frame; the remaining (k_base-1)*N frames are distributed proportional to per-segment mean dynamics (water-filling, cap dynamics_keyframe_max=4); for long videos (k_base=1) allocation is the identity. (3) Placement — REFINEMENT R1 (stratified, replaces B's global top-k): each segment's k frames are selected by splitting the segment's frame_indices into k equal contiguous temporal sub-windows and taking the argmax-d(t) frame within EACH sub-window, re-sorted temporally. This guarantees >= duration/k temporal spread (the mechanism's entire purpose) and bounds any single dynamics spike (camera shake, lighting flicker) to 1 of k frames, whereas B's global top-k could cluster all k frames on one 0.5s burst and recreate the blindness at a new location. REFINEMENT R2 (non-degenerate fallback): when tsm/motion are missing or zero-range (flat static videos — exactly the low-motion property-crime class), d(t) is treated as unavailable and the k frames are placed at EVENLY SPACED positions across the segment (np.linspace over the segment's frames); B's original "uniform 0.5 then top-k" silently degenerates to the head-slice (top-k of a constant array returns the first k indices), recreating the v97 defect precisely where the fallback fires most. Everything downstream is byte-identical: same contiguous batches, same comparative prompt, same 0.3 threshold, same _merge_adjacent, candidate_top_k=3, same v51 half-max boundary detection on the untouched 0.75*CLIP+0.25*MIL curve, same v95/v96 confidence modulators, hard NMS, gates. The independent scan_segment path is NOT touched.

WHY NOT MERGED WITH A (CABS): the hard constraint is ONE controlled change per loop; scan-evidence (B) and boundary-selection (A) are independent mechanisms whose effects would be unattributable in a single eval. More decisively, the two are not independent in value: A's completeness reference vlm_fit is built by binarizing the FCCS per-segment scores — the very scores B proves are computed from the first 0.5s of each segment. A inherits the evidence blindness B fixes, so B is logically upstream and must land first; CABS is queued as the next loop, where its vlm_fit will be computed from dynamics-informed scores (and its hysteresis design re-reviewed against the new score distribution).
structured.rationale: Both proposals have code-verified root causes, so the decision turns on failure-pool coverage, dependency order, and risk. (1) POOL: B attacks the dominant bottleneck — ~15 zero-IoU wrong-location videos (28.8% of candidates per v97) — which A does nothing for; A attacks the 19-video IoU 0.05-0.3 band (~8-10 verified sub-window cases). B also PARTIALLY helps A's pool: once events are visible in the scan images, comparative scores localize the true extent better, improving candidates and (via the existing v51 half-max on the untouched curve) some boundaries; the converse is false — no boundary-selection rule can recover a video whose true segment the VLM never saw. (2) DEPENDENCY: A's new signal vlm_fit is the FCCS per-segment score curve binarized at 0.3 — computed from the blind head-frames. A's own Fighting047 example is survivorship (the extent happened to be visible); for sub-window cases where the event is mid-segment, CABS would pull boundaries toward a wrong VLM extent, gated only by hysteresis. Fixing the evidence layer first raises A's future ceiling and de-risks its signal. (3) RISK: boundary-selection replacements regressed twice (v59, v65); A's symmetry+hysteresis argument is plausible but its J = contrast x duration_fit^gamma x vlm_fit^beta introduces 3 interacting hyperparameters whose product behavior is untested — nearer the tuning regime. B is FM-clean by construction (see risks) and its change category (wholesale same-VLM mechanism replacement inside the scan) is exactly what v97 validated as safe (+0.0123). (4) EVIDENCE QUALITY: B's defect is numerically re-verified end-to-end this session (slice site, temporal ordering, fps=2, target=18>=12); it explains v97's own lesson verbatim. v56's comparative gain (+0.006) and v97's (+0.0123) were achieved DESPITE showing the VLM only segment heads — i.e., pure calibration gains; the evidence half is the untapped one, and no decision-side change (coverage, calibration, revoting, fusion, boundary rules) can recover events invisible in the input. DGEA is the first change in 45+ versions that increases the VLM's effective perceptual coverage per unit time instead of changing a decision rule — the training-free analog of Holmes-VAU's Anomaly-focused Temporal Sampler, with the trained scorer replaced by two already-computed dynamics signals (v95 TSM novelty = semantic scene change, robust to pixel flicker; motion energy = pixel change; per-video min-max makes the combination robust across static and dynamic videos). It also directly respects v97's latency lesson (image tokens dominate): the budget invariant makes latency exactly neutral. The two refinements are consensus hardening of B's own design, not new mechanisms: R1 (stratified sub-window argmax) guarantees the temporal spread that is the mechanism's purpose and caps outlier influence at 1/k frames; R2 (even-spacing fallback) eliminates the degenerate case where flat-dynamics videos — the static Shoplifting/Stealing class the mechanism most needs to help — would silently recreate the head-slice.

Robustness: ±10% on the half-max multiplier gives 0.1926/0.1767 — always >= +0.015, so the direction does not depend on a lucky constant (and I propose mult=1.0 anyway = v51's exact formula, zero tuned parameters). Per-video: 9 wins / 6 losses; wins are large (Arson041 best-IoU 0.23→0.86, Fighting042 0.41→0.49, Fighting047 0.17→0.28, Vandalism036 0.25→0.31 crossing TP@0.3); losses are small and mostly non-crossing (Arrest001 0.87→0.83 stays TP@0.7); the ONLY threshold-crossing loss is Arson035 flipping TP@0.5 (0.55→0.47). structured.mechanism: One new post-processing stage inserted near the END of detect() (after Stage 7 ensemble classification, 7b curve correction, MIL-sanity, and the category confidence gate; before the final dict projection at pipeline.py:998). For each final detection whose duration is already < its category max_dur from CATEGORY_DURATION_PRIORS[cat]['expected_duration'][1]: (1) fetch the full-video relative CLIP curve for the detection's (final, ensemble-decided) category via the EXISTING frame_scorer.get_category_scores(video_data, category) cache — the exact rel = cat/(cat+normal) curve, never modified; (2) compute the v51 half-max level hm = (peak + percentile20)/2 over the WHOLE video curve (verbatim reuse of the v51 formula, mult=1.0, no new constant); (3) from the curve indices aligned with the detection's t_start/t_end (via searchsorted on video_data['timestamps']), walk left/right greedily while curve stays >= hm; (4) REJECT-CAP: if the grown span would exceed the category max_dur, keep the original boundaries untouched; otherwise replace t_start/t_end. result.content:
**Critique of B (ECE)**

**(a) FM audit: clean.** FM1 untouched — rel curve read-only; ECE operates on final detection outputs, the same validated change-class as v95/v96 (read-only post-hoc modulation of fixed detections), with the v53 guard philosophy mirrored (expand-only, reject-cap by max_dur). Grep confirms no prior expansion/region-growing attempt in the logs; v52/v53 were shrinks, so this is not a retry. One real interaction: v66 LogOIC/v60 tightening deliberately narrowed over-wide dets, and ECE can partially re-expand them — but B's simulation starts from final post-tightening JSONs, so this interaction is already priced into +0.0307.

**One inaccuracy to fix, not fatal:** B claims "verbatim v51 formula." Code check (pipeline.py:1483-1485, 1466): v51 computes (peak+p20)/2 over the **local candidate window on the fused 0.75CLIP+0.25MIL curve**; B computes it over the **whole-video rel category curve**. Same formula, different signal and domain. Mandate: implement *exactly what was simulated* (rel curve, whole-video) — do NOT "align with v51" post-hoc, as that voids the offline evidence; correct the docstring instead.

**(b) Architecture-level: yes.** It removes v51's structural search-window cap (~2x candidate duration) that makes long events unrecoverable — a regime change with zero new tuned constants, not threshold tuning.

**(c) Gain plausibility: strongest evidence any loop has had.** Baseline reproduced exactly on the official evaluator; delta is deterministic (zero stochasticity added); robust to ±10% mult (+0.015 to +0.031). The ±0.03 VLM noise caveat is correctly handled via deterministic flag-ON/OFF A/B plus byte-identical off-path assertion. Honest caveats B already owns: 2/65 cached curves missing; Arson041 gain rides on category-agnostic matching.

**(d) Latency: ~zero.** Cached curve, O(n) index walk.

**Verdict: ACCEPT B over my TPV — unconditionally.** Decisive reason: B's own offline analysis measured VideoMAE window sep-AUC at 0.473 (saturated), which means TPV's mandatory pre-validation gate (>60% inside>outside) would almost certainly **reject my own proposal in 5 minutes**. ECE attacks the same boundary-imprecision mass with evaluator-verified gain, zero cost, zero risk beyond a bounded cap. Sequence: run ECE as the next loop against the v97 baseline (FCCS flag-off path, given v98's no-fire); mandate the [ECE] log line for the grep gate, off-path JSON diff, and exact-simulation fidelity. TPV is withdrawn unless a future trained-signal audit contradicts the 0.473 finding.

A's only defense is "non-collapsed signal," but non-collapsed for video classification ≠ temporally discriminative: a 16s-window/8s-stride classifier trained on full-video labels yields saturated scores on abnormal videos (our offline oracle check: VideoMAE window sep-AUC ≈0.473, below chance; scores saturate high everywhere, so inside-GT vs outside-GT contrast is near-zero). A's own FCCS lesson states coverage cannot fix candidates when the underlying signal cannot discriminate the true segment from neighbors — TPV swaps in a weaker signal. This is the exact ECE insertion template, attacking the OPPOSITE failure mode: ECE extends shrunk detections; EUBC contracts over-wide ones.

For each final detection a=[t_s,t_e] with category cat (skip None/'Normal'):
1. Read the cached whole-video relative CLIP curve rel = cat/(cat+normal) via frame_scorer.get_category_scores (read-only, never re-fused) and the consecutive-frame cosine similarities sims[i]=cos(feat_i, feat_{i+1}) computed once in Stage 1 from the already-cached clip_features (zero extra CLIP/VLM calls — same reuse pattern as v95's TSM).
2. Peak anchor: P = argmax of rel within [t_s,t_e] (the point of strongest anomaly evidence).
3. Coherence walk (EventVAD's event-unit signal): adaptive threshold thr = median(sims) − 1.0×1.4826×MAD(sims) (canonical robust z=1; the 1.4826 is the standard MAD normal-consistency constant, not a tuned knob). Walk L leftward from P while sims[L−1] ≥ thr (frames L−1,L visually coherent → same event unit); walk R rightward while sims[R] ≥ thr. Coherence span = [ts[L], ts[R]].
4. Plateau-union guard (reuses the exact v51 half-max LEVEL formula, zero new constants): within the detection compute hm=(max+p20)/2 of rel; plateau = {rel ≥ hm}. Guarded span = [min(L_time, plateau_left), max(R_time, plateau_right)] — i.e., never cut extent that the curve's own half-max evidence supports. (The offline ablation proves this guard is load-bearing: without it, Arson009 over-shrinks IoU 0.164→0.0.)
5. Contraction-only clip to [t_s,t_e]; FIRE only if new_dur < 0.75×det_dur (materiality — tiny trims are no-ops) AND new_dur ≥ min_segment(cat) (existing CATEGORY_DURATION_PRIORS constant). Proposal submitted. Summary of the work:

**Analysis (all evidence deterministic):**
- Read the mandatory logs (v86-v99 summaries, v95-v99 idea files, roadmap spec) and the core code (`pipeline.py` detect/Stage-5 boundary machinery at lines 738-1698, `config.py`, `frame_scorer.py`, `post_processor.py`).

- Ran 8 real WebSearch queries + 3 WebFetch deep-dives (T3AL, EventVAD, Learning Event Completeness). Key find: EventVAD (training-free, 82% AUC UCF-Crime) segments video into coherent event units via consecutive-frame cosine dissimilarity + MAD-adaptive thresholding.

**Proposed idea — EUBC (Event-Unit Boundary Contraction):** a post-hoc, contraction-only stage at the exact ECE insertion point (after the confidence gate at `pipeline.py:993-996`, before dict projection at `:998`), behind one config switch. Full plan, FM1-FM4/FM5 avoidance analysis, and file-level implementation steps are in the StructuredOutput record.

structured.title: EUBC: Event-Unit Boundary Contraction — post-hoc contraction of over-wide final detections onto the coherent visual event unit containing the anomaly peak, via consecutive-frame CLIP cosine-similarity with MAD-adaptive thresholding, half-max-plateau-guarded and contraction-only (ECE's mirror image for the opposite, currently unaddressed boundary failure mode)
structured.mechanism:
One new post-processing stage at the END of detect() — after Stage 7b clip_score_curve_correction, MIL-sanity, and the category confidence gate (pipeline.py:989-996), before the final dict projection (pipeline.py:998) — behind a single new switch ScoringConfig.event_unit_boundary_contraction: bool = False (False = byte-identical prior behavior). This is the exact ECE insertion template, attacking the OPPOSITE failure mode: ECE extends shrunk detections; EUBC contracts over-wide ones.

For each final detection a=[t_s,t_e] with category cat (skip None/'Normal'):
1. Read the cached whole-video relative CLIP curve rel = cat/(cat+normal) via frame_scorer.get_category_scores (read-only, never re-fused) and the consecutive-frame cosine similarities sims[i]=cos(feat_i, feat_{i+1}) computed once in Stage 1 from the already-cached clip_features (zero extra CLIP/VLM calls — same reuse pattern as v95's TSM).
2. Peak anchor: P = argmax of rel within [t_s,t_e] (the point of strongest anomaly evidence).
3. Coherence walk (EventVAD's event-unit signal): adaptive threshold thr = median(sims) − 1.0×1.4826×MAD(sims) (canonical robust z=1; the 1.4826 is the standard MAD normal-consistency constant, not a tuned knob). Walk L leftward from P while sims[L−1] ≥ thr (frames L−1,L visually coherent → same event unit); walk R rightward while sims[R] ≥ thr. Coherence span = [ts[L], ts[R]].
4. Plateau-union guard (reuses the exact v51 half-max LEVEL formula, zero new constants): within the detection compute hm=(max+p20)/2 of rel; plateau = {rel ≥ hm}. Guarded span = [min(L_time, plateau_left), max(R_time, plateau_right)] — i.e., never cut extent that the curve's own half-max evidence supports. (The offline ablation proves this guard is load-bearing: without it, Arson009 over-shrinks IoU 0.164→0.0.)
5. Contraction-only clip to [t_s,t_e]; FIRE only if new_dur < 0.75×det_dur (materiality — tiny trims are no-ops) AND new_dur ≥ min_segment(cat) (existing CATEGORY_DURATION_PRIORS constant). Otherwise no-op. Confidence, category, detection COUNT, order, NMS, merge, and every upstream stage byte-identical; no re-NMS; no VLM/CLIP recompute. Per-detection [EUBC] log line reporting fired/no-op reason, mirroring the [ECE] FM5 gate discipline (eval runner must refuse metrics when the activation grep count == 0 and the run had contractible detections).
Self-limiting by construction: flat coherence (property crimes, whole-video-spanning units) → span ≈ video or ≥ 0.75×det → no-op; coherent detection (span ≈ det) → no-op; only demonstrably multi-scene detections contract.
structured.rationale:
Targets the largest UNADDRESSED failure mass. My per-video IoU analysis of the v97 full run (67 GT segments, official matching semantics): 21 segments IoU=0 (wrong-location — FCCS's pending job), 27 segments at IoU 0.1-0.5 (boundary mass). Splitting the boundary mass by detection/GT duration ratio: ~7 are SHRUNK (ratio<0.7 — ECE's pending job, simulated +0.031) and 16+ are OVER-WIDE (ratio>1.5, up to 11x — e.g., Burglary037 GT 5s in a 55s detection, Arson009 GT 3.2s in 19.5s, RoadAccidents GT 2-4s in 7-15.2s, Shoplifting GT 4s in 12.5-18.7s). ECE cannot help these (it only grows); v52/v53 taught us unconditional curve-based contraction regresses; Stage 7b skips everything ≤ max_dur (and category max_dur priors are 10-40s, far looser than these 2-5s events). This bucket is structurally unaddressed: no current stage can shrink a 10s detection of a 3s event when the category max_dur is 20s.

Why coherence-based contraction breaks the pattern: the detection is wide because it mixes multiple visual event units (approach/event/aftermath); the true event is ONE coherent unit. EventVAD (training-free VAD, 82.03% AUC on UCF-Crime vs our ~0.70) demonstrates that consecutive-frame feature divergence with MAD-adaptive thresholding recovers exactly these event units on UCF-Crime. v95 already validated the SSM/novelty structure in this codebase (used only for confidence). EUBC is the first use of an independent VISUAL-coherence extent signal for boundary extent — the curve that produced the wide detection is used only as a floor guard, never as the contraction driver (the exact v52 lesson).

Deterministic offline evidence (ECE-grade, produced on the pipeline's own signals — fps=2 motion-filtered grid, ViT-L-14 + learned prompt weights, rel curve — via the repo's own VideoPreprocessor/VideoAnomalyExpert classes): on 12 representative videos (7 over-wide failures with ratio>2 + 5 well-localized controls): total IoU +0.645, ZERO regressions; fired 3/7 over-wide (RoadAccidents125 0.243→0.529, Robbery106 0.182→0.308, Shooting002 0.245→0.305), self-limiting no-ops on all ambiguous cases (Burglary037 flat whole-video coherence, Arson009/Shoplifting020/Vandalism017 unit≈detection), and one control IMPROVED (Explosion004 0.625→0.800, other 4 controls untouched). Sensitivity sweep over k_mad∈{0.5,1,1.5,2} × materiality∈{0.65,0.75,0.85}: total delta always in [+0.509, +0.686] — no knife-edge dependence on the constants. Guard ablation: without the plateau-union guard, Arson009 over-shrinks 0.164→0.0 — the guard is necessary and the guarded version never regressed in any swept configuration.

result.content:
VERDICT: Reject B as a replacement for EUBC; conditional merge as a strictly-later loop, only with mandated amendments.

(a) FM check: FM1/FM2/FM3/FM4 are avoided by construction (read-only curves, terminal insertion, frozen count/order/confidence) — same safety class as ECE/EUBC. But B repeats two tried-and-failed mechanisms. Its "static" term is literally inner-outer contrast — the OIC/LogOIC family this repo burned three consecutive loops on (v65 LogOIC smoke mAP=0.0632; v66/v67 LogOIC tightening; pipeline.py:380 "contrast*duration_fit… 连续三轮全部让 mAP 变差"). rawResult.content:
Proposal submitted via StructuredOutput. Key findings from this loop:

1. **Critical codebase discovery**: the archived v97 full run (current "best" 0.16155) contains zero `[FCCS]` activation lines but 24 `[CLIP pre-screen]` and 65 `[LLM scan]` old-path lines — it ran **flag-off**. Corroborated by the v98 idea file's own conclusion ("the v97 runs were executed WITHOUT the flag"). The verified live baseline is still ~0.149 (v94-lineage); the full-coverage comparative architecture has **never been evaluated live**, and v97's "coverage can't fix wrong-location" lesson was inferred from a flag-off run.

2. **Bottleneck refinement**: v97-log analysis shows post-merge candidate counts are only 1-3/video (top_k truncation fired ~4/65), so wrong-location is a **judgment** failure (true segment never out-scores neighbors under saturated 0-1 ratings), not a truncation failure. Combined with the 84.1% keyframe-coverage finding, the VLM already *sees* the events — discrimination elicitation is the lever.

3. **Proposal (v102 RFCS)**: one-switch Stage-4 architecture — forced-ranking comparative judgment per batch (binary ANOMALOUS/NORMAL gate + total order, preserving junk compression and the Normal-video path) plus a single global playoff call (≤5 finalists × 3 keyframes) for cross-batch calibration. Avoids FM1-FM4 by construction, includes all six FM5 hardening mandates in the metric-extraction code path, honest band +0.00 to +0.03 standalone, composes with the queued ECE/EUBC/BRP flag-ON runs toward 0.20-0.23.

structured.title: v102 RFCS: Full-Coverage Forced-Ranking Comparative Scan with Global Playoff — hierarchical local-to-global forced-choice judgment replaces absolute 0-1 rating in Stage 4 (one switch; first FM5-hardened live firing of the never-evaluated full-coverage architecture)
structured.mechanism:
ONE controlled architecture change to Stage 4 candidate generation, behind a single new switch DiscoveryConfig.full_coverage_ranking_scan (default False = byte-identical prior behavior). Same segments, same keyframes, same contiguous 8-segment batches (16 at 1 keyframe for >60-segment videos), same coverage, same call count. Only the response schema changes: the VLM must (a) mark each segment ANOMALOUS or NORMAL using the others as the in-video baseline (binary gate — this is what preserves v97's junk-compression win and the Normal-video precision path), then (b) output a FORCED TOTAL ORDER over only the ANOMALOUS segments (ties forbidden). structured.literature: 1) T*: Re-thinking Temporal Search for Long-Form Video Understanding (CVPR 2025, arXiv 2504.02259) — adaptive zooming-in temporal search at a fixed 32-frame budget improves GPT-4o 50.5->53.1 and LLaVA-OneVision-72B 56.5->62.4; borrowed mechanism: coarse-to-fine frame-budget reallocation instead of uniform sampling for MLLM temporal tasks. 2) Holmes-VAU (CVPR 2025 Highlight, arXiv 2412.06171) — Anomaly-focused Temporal Sampler: score-guided non-uniform temporal density is THE mechanism for long-video anomaly localization (UCF-Crime AUC 88.96%); HZG solves its bootstrap (it needs a trained irregularity scorer) by using the zero-cost comparative coarse pass as the scorer. 3) BSN (ECCV 2018) / BMN (ICCV 2019) / PBRNet (AAAI 2020) — the canonical two-stage propose-then-refine TAL cascade: cheap proposals, expensive re-scoring of a shortlist; HZG is this pattern with the VLM as both stages. 4) MGFN (CVPR 2023) — multi-granularity evidence for VAD. 5) TSPO (AAAI 2026, arXiv 2508.04369) — learned temporal sampling policies improve MLLM video understanding; sampling granularity is a first-class design axis. 6) T3AL (ECCV 2024, arXiv 2404.05426) — region-level reasoning for zero-shot TAL. 7) UTAL-GNN (arXiv 2508.19647, unsupervised TAL via embedding-norm dynamics) — consulted and rejected: visual-only dynamics signals are dead for flat-CLIP categories in this repo (VideoMAE window sep-AUC 0.473). 8) FreeZAD (arXiv 2501.13795) — LogOIC/multi-threshold lineage already tried (v65-68); its Prototype-Centric test-time adaptation is too heavy. 9) Internal: v56 comparative judging isolated +0.006; v57 non-exclusive schema; v97 FCCS code (reused as pass 1) with my audit finding its full eval never fired (archived log shows [Directed scan], zero [FCCS] lines); v101 keyframe-coverage analysis (84.1% — coverage without readable density); roadmap bottleneck #1 (28.8% wrong-location).

CRITIQUE OF A (v102 HZG):

(a) Failure modes: FM1/FM2 genuinely clean; FM3 absent. But the FM4 claim is overstated. The zoom pass re-adjudicates segments the coarse pass already scored, and fine-replaces-coarse can push a coarse-accepted segment (>0.3) below threshold — that is re-voting on an inclusion-relevant measurement, squarely in the v92 danger zone. "Different granularity = new evidence" is a partial defense, not absence-by-construction. Cheap fix: make fine scores upgrade-only (floor = coarse for segments already >0.3); the cascade keeps its recall win and loses the flip risk. Deeper issue is A's own risk #3: pass 1 is the never-fired v97 FCCS, so HZG stacks an unproven base plus a new stage as one "inseparable" unit — no attribution if it fails, and the threshold-free top-6 rank-net re-imports exactly the junk v97's comparative compression removed. The pre-live gate is the proposal's best feature; adopt it unconditionally.

(b) Architecture-level: yes — a real cascade, constants are schema not tuned thresholds.

(c) Gain plausibility: +0.015–0.04 rests on an untested perceptual assumption: that 8 stills at 0.75s make 1–2s gestures "readable" to a VLM doing no motion reasoning. T* evidence is long-form search, not 6s windows. In-repo evidence cuts the other way: v101 shows 84.1% of true segments are already shown a GT frame, and v97 merged candidates are 1–3/video — the bottleneck is judgment/elicitation, not sight. That favors RFCS's axis.

(d) Latency: honest, but image-token dominated per v97's lesson; 3 zoom calls at 16 images on long videos risks breaching 150s. Ladder mitigates.

DECISION: Merge, sequenced — do not accept HZG over RFCS for v102. RFCS runs first: it is cheaper (near-neutral latency), one controlled elicitation change, and targets the in-repo-evidenced bottleneck. From A, adopt wholesale: the pre-live gate (recall-of-shortlist measurement on named wrong-location videos), named-video smoke gates, and runner-side FM5 enforcement. Queue HZG as v103 with two hardenings: (i) upgrade-only fine scoring (kills the FM4 adjacency); (ii) build its zoom shortlist from RFCS's playoff global order rather than coarse absolute scores — eliminating the junk-outranking risk and making the two compose instead of compete. If the panel prefers HZG first, acceptance is conditional on (i) plus the gate firing >=0.25.

PASS 1 — COARSE FIELD (reuses the v97 FCCS code verbatim, first-ever gated live firing): every 6s segment of the video is comparatively rated at 2 keyframes/segment (1 for >60-segment videos) in contiguous-time batches of 8x2=16 images via the existing scan_full_coverage internals, refactored into a thin behavior-preserving wrapper over a new _scan_full_coverage_scored() that returns (time-ordered segments, per-segment anomaly_score for ALL segments). Same v57 non-exclusive segment_scores schema, same 0.3 semantics, same category_hint, same _scan_comparative_batch_guarded truncation guard (split-retry-once, then independent scan_segment fallback). Coarse elicitation stays ABSOLUTE-RATING comparative: v56's +0.006 was measured with exactly this mode, and a calibrated score field is required for shortlist selection — changing it AND adding the zoom would be two uncontrolled variables.

structured.title: v102 HZG-FC: Hierarchical Zoom-in Grounding with Forced-Choice Zoom Verification — a two-stage coarse-to-fine VLM cascade for Stage 4 (JOINT A+B CONSENSUS: A's cascade skeleton + density mechanism adopted as the architecture; B's forced relative/binary elicitation moved INTO the zoom pass, the one decision point where it is load-bearing and non-fabricating; B's coarse-pass forced ranking and playoff score ladder DEFERRED with named trigger conditions)
structured.mechanism:
ONE controlled architecture change to Stage 4 candidate generation, behind a single new switch DiscoveryConfig.hierarchical_zoom_scan (default False = byte-identical prior behavior; pipeline branch order `if _hzg: ... elif _fccs: ...` so the two switches never double-fire). Stage 4 becomes a two-stage coarse-to-fine cascade (BSN PGM->PEM propose-then-refine ported to VLM scanning; T*/Zoom-Zero granularity reallocation made training-free):

PASS 1 — COARSE FIELD (reuses the v97 FCCS code verbatim, first-ever gated live firing): every 6s segment of the video is comparatively rated at 2 keyframes/segment (1 for >60-segment videos) in contiguous-time batches of 8x2=16 images via the existing scan_full_coverage internals, refactored into a thin behavior-preserving wrapper over a new _scan_full_coverage_scored() that returns (time-ordered segments, per-segment anomaly_score for ALL segments). Same v57 non-exclusive segment_scores schema, same 0.3 semantics, same category_hint, same _scan_comparative_batch_guarded truncation guard (split-retry-once, then independent scan_segment fallback). Coarse elicitation stays ABSOLUTE-RATING comparative: v56's +0.006 was measured with exactly this mode, and a calibrated score field is required for shortlist selection — changing it AND adding the zoom would be two uncontrolled variables.

PASS 2 — FORCED-CHOICE ZOOM (the new mechanism, A's density + B's elicitation at the decisive measurement): (a) SHORTLIST: Z = union of {coarse > 0.3} and the top-zoom_top_m(6) segments by coarse score regardless of threshold (ties -> earlier time), capped at zoom_max_segments(6) by score desc, then TIME-SORTED. The rank-net catches true events comparatively mid-ranked at 0.15-0.3 that the threshold silently drops. (b) DENSE PAIRWISE RE-JUDGMENT: pair Z in time order (temporal neighbors are the documented confounders — the v97 lesson's true-vs-neighbor failure), zoom_pair_size=2 x zoom_keyframes=8 = 16 images/call (identical payload to the proven v97 batches; ~0.75s spacing inside a 6s segment — enough density to SEE a 1-2s conceal/impact gesture that 2 frames 3s apart structurally miss; odd |Z| leaves one singleton 8-image call, verdict only). NEW ZOOM SCHEMA replacing A's absolute-rating re-score with B's forced elicitation: per segment {"segment": id, "anomalous": true/false, "confidence": 0-1, "description": "max 8 words"} plus pair-level "more_anomalous": id (ties forbidden). The binary verdict is judged against the in-video baseline established in pass 1; the forced pick is the comparison-forcing elicitation (RankGPT/pairwise-preference lineage) that breaks saturation inside the 2-segment comparative frame. DECODE (no fabricated merit ordering): anomalous=false -> fine score 0.05 (the existing 0.3-gate semantics, below acceptance — a gate, not an invented rank); anomalous=true -> fine score = the VLM's OWN confidence (honest scores, unlike B's structural ladder); "more_anomalous" used only as a tie-break when confidences are within 0.05. (c) NO-LOSS MERGE: reuse _scan_comparative_batch_guarded's guard logic for zoom pairs; pair parse failure -> KEEP the coarse scores for that pair's segments and log (explicit no-loss rule; never a silent zero). final_score[i] = fine[i] for Z members whose pair parsed OK else coarse[i].

structured.rationale:
CONSENSUS LOGIC — why this exact merge is the single proposal both researchers sign. SHARED DIAGNOSIS (both proposals agree, code-verified this session): (1) the dominant loss bucket is wrong-location candidates (~15 zero-IoU abnormal videos; roadmap 28.8%); (2) the v97 FCCS full-coverage comparative scan — both proposals' foundation — has NEVER fired live (v97/v98 flag omissions confirmed by 0 [FCCS] lines in archived logs; the 0.16155 "best" is a directed-scan number); (3) the v101 keyframe-coverage analysis shows the VLM is already SHOWN a frame inside GT(+/-0.5s) for 84.1% of true segments — the bottleneck is JUDGMENT, not sight.

WHERE B'S RFCS IS WEAKER (A's critique, adopted): (i) B's own log analysis shows post-merge candidate counts are 1-3/video and candidate_top_k truncation fired only ~4/65 — so within-batch ORDER, the thing coarse-pass forced ranking changes, has almost no addressable mass; the failure is the true segment never being flagged above neighbors, not being outranked after flagging. (ii) B's rank->score map and playoff ladder FABRICATE absolute scores (batch rank-1 -> 1.0; global rank-1 -> 0.9 regardless of the VLM's own confidence), and coarse_score is load-bearing downstream: it feeds candidate top-k ordering (pipeline.py:974), base confidence (pipeline.py:1848 "80% of LLM coarse_score"), and is copied verbatim as confidence on the low-CLIP path (pipeline.py:1657/1668/1903). Under greedy-match evaluation's global confidence sort, a fabricated 0.9 on a quiet video's least-bad segment can outrank honest TPs on other videos — an FM-adjacent distortion neither researcher can bound offline. (iii) Decisively, B concedes ranking is "arbitrary when the VLM truly cannot discriminate" — i.e., elicitation re-allocates EXISTING discrimination but creates none; for the target bucket the discrimination does not exist at 2 keyframes 3s apart (a 1-2s gesture falls between frames), so ranking-only has ~zero expected TP recovery where the mAP mass is.

WHERE A'S HZG IS WEAKER (B's critique, adopted): (i) the zoom rank-net inherits the coarse field's saturation — if junk ties at 0.9, top-6-by-score is arbitrary among the tied mass; this is real and is why the pre-live gate (below) measures rank-net recall on the named wrong-location videos and KILLS the loop at <0.25 before any full-eval spend (v56's measured junk compression under comparative rating is the counter-prior that makes the gate worth running). (ii) A's zoom re-scoring used the SAME absolute 0-1 rating that v56 documented saturating, on a thin 2-segment comparative baseline — the weakest link in A's own design.

THE MERGE REPAIRS EACH WITH THE OTHER: A's density is the only proposed mechanism that creates NEW discrimination ability (T*, CVPR 2025 — verified live: adaptive zoom at fixed frame budget improves MLLM video temporal tasks +2.6-5.9 points over uniform sampling; Zoom-Zero, ICLR 2026 — verified live: coarse-to-fine temporal zoom +5.2% NExT-GQA grounding, +6.4% long-video avg, trained with RL — HZG-FC is the training-free analogue), and B's forced binary/relative elicitation (RankGPT EMNLP 2023; pairwise-preference judges 2024 — both verified) is the saturation-immune way to COLLECT that discrimination: a binary "do you SEE the gesture?" verdict at 0.75s spacing is a perceptual verification task with a definite answer (FM3-safe), while the forced pair pick extracts the relative judgment without inventing absolute merit. B's global-calibration concern (cross-batch drift) is subsumed, not dropped: every finalist is re-measured on ONE common dense binary scale, which IS the global recalibration stage — at 8 keyframes instead of the playoff's 3, where gestures are actually visible. CHANGE-CLASS SAFETY: this is the v97-cleared class (same VLM, same segments, wholesale replacement of the initial inclusion mechanism) with one added second-stage measurement INSIDE the cascade before any decision is frozen; it attacks the bucket that the queued terminal stages (ECE +0.0311 sim, EUBC +0.015-0.04 sim, BRP +0.006 sim) structurally cannot touch, so it composes instead of colliding.

Downside is bounded: pair-failure keeps coarse (no silent zeros), count/rank machinery unchanged, scores stay honest (no fabricated ladder), and the pre-live gate kills the loop before any full-eval spend if the rank-net cannot see the target bucket. FM2 (count/greedy-match): bounded — top_k=3/_merge_adjacent/hard NMS/gates unchanged; score replacement happens INSIDE the cascade before any decision is frozen; binary down-voting reduces candidate count, the safe direction under greedy matching. FM3: absent — single deterministic temp=0 call per batch and per zoom pair; no sampling diversity; no timestamp extraction (segment scores only, v57-style schema); the binary verdict is a perceptual verification with a definite answer, the task class v90/v96 showed is robust. FM4: absent — coarse scores are intermediate representations, not decisions; inclusion is decided exactly once from final scores; nothing frozen is flipped (v92's revoting acted on a frozen pool). NEW/ACCEPTED RISKS: (1) Rank-net saturation miss (B's strongest critique of A): if junk ties at 0.9 and the true segment falls below top-6, the zoom never sees it — the pre-live gate measures EXACTLY this on the named wrong-location videos and kills the loop at <0.25 recall before any full-eval spend; v56's measured junk compression is the counter-prior making the gate worth running; this is the single largest risk and it is cheaply pre-measured. (6) FM5 (the #1 recurring defect, 5 consecutive failures): all seven mandates are in the runner's metric-extraction code path and launch protocol, not a checklist. DEFERRAL RECORD (B's components, not rejected): coarse-pass forced ranking fires only if the pre-live gate shows extreme saturation AND rank-net recall < 0.25 (the loop's kill condition) — then it becomes the next loop's candidate fix for the coarse field; the playoff score ladder is dropped outright (fabricated confidences flow into greedy-match global ranking via pipeline.py:974/:1848/:1657 — unbounded distortion), its global-calibration intent subsumed by the common dense binary re-measurement of all finalists.
structured.latency_impact: Net +10 to +22 s/video vs the ~128s v94 budget, i.e. ~140-150s, comparable to the accepted v97-era measurements (141.47s) and honestly disclosed as above the 128s target band. Math: pass 1 ~3.7 calls/video at 16 images (identical to the v97 FCCS design; replaces the 10-18 directed calls); pass 2 adds ceil(|Z|/2) <= 3 calls at 2x8=16 images (odd |Z| -> one 8-image half call); total image tokens roughly +40-48 per video over pass-1-only, worst case ~112 images/video. Summary of work:

The proposal — **TBA: Transition-Anchored Boundary Alignment**: a terminal post-hoc stage that snaps v51 half-max edges (bounded ±2s radius, MAD-gated no-op default, EventVAD's median+3·MAD rule) to peaks of a cached multi-signal transition field (v95 TSM novelty + motion gradient, zero new model calls, <50ms/video), attacking the edge-OFFSET axis of the 39% boundary-imprecision bucket that neither ECE (grow) nor EUBC (contract) can touch, with deterministic sim-gated adjudication on cached v97 JSONs before any live spend and v102-grade FM5 launcher armor.

structured.title: TBA: Transition-Anchored Boundary Alignment — MAD-gated snapping of v51 half-max edges to a cached multi-signal visual-transition field (TSM novelty + motion gradient), attacking the unaddressed edge-OFFSET axis of the 39% boundary-imprecision bucket
structured.mechanism: One new terminal post-processing stage in `Pipeline.detect()` (/Users/zzl/PycharmProjects/vad/video_anomaly_detection/pipeline.py), inserted immediately after the v100 EUBC block (pipeline.py:1066-1068) and before the final dict projection (pipeline.py:1070), behind a single switch `ScoringConfig.transition_boundary_alignment: bool = False` (flag-off = byte-identical prior behavior). Flat-field guard: robust MAD of E < eps -> explicit no-op. (2) PER-BOUNDARY SNAP, independently for t_b in {t_s, t_e}: window W = [t_b - R, t_b + R], R = min(transition_max_snap=2.0s, transition_snap_frac=0.25 x det_dur); candidate anchors = local maxima of E inside W on the timestamp grid; SIGNIFICANCE GATE (EventVAD's exact robust rule): anchor >= median(E_W) + transition_mad_k(3.0) x 1.4826 x MAD(E_W); if any significant anchor exists, snap t_b to the NEAREST one (ties -> higher E); else keep the v51 boundary unchanged. (3) STRUCTURAL GUARDS: t_s < t_e with det_dur >= CATEGORY_DURATION_PRIORS[cat]['min_segment'] else revert that snap; boundary-collision guard — a snap is rejected if it would move the edge inside any other final detection's interval (count/order/confidence/category byte-identical; no re-NMS; FM2-frozen). (4) LOGGING/FM5: per-detection [TBA] snap/no-op line + exactly one [TBA] summary per video at ALL return paths; activation gate inside the runner's metric-extraction code path (refuse evaluation_report.json when flag-on and summaries != succeeded); verbatim persisted COMMAND.txt; and per the v102 FM5 root cause, a MANDATORY non-opt-in pre-launch argv assertion (launch command generated from a flag-interpolating template; hard abort before any VLM spend if the flag string is absent). structured.rationale: The 39% boundary-imprecision bucket (IoU 0.1-0.5) is the largest loss mass after wrong-location, and code evidence shows a systematic cause no stage addresses: `_clip_boundary_detection` (pipeline.py:1751-1783) crosses half-max on a boxcar-SMOOTHED curve, which shifts edges outward by ~half the kernel and further on gradual-rise curves — an edge-OFFSET error. TBA is the third, orthogonal axis: align each edge to the nearest SIGNIFICANT peak of a category-independent transition field.
